item.title: Corner Kitchen Cabinet Storage: How to Choose a System That Fits
item.description: Corner cabinets are awkward because the space inside is often larger than the opening you reach it through. A rotating shelf that suits one corner can be wrong for another, and a pull-out built for a blind corner may not fit a cabinet with a two-part folding door. Buying the organizer first is how people end up with a box of hardware that cannot pass through their own door. This guide names the corner type first, measures the opening and every obstruction, compares the three common fixes and ends with a fallback for tight or rented cabinets plus a one-page decision sheet.
